description: We are a team of friends and beginner programmers interested in space exploration and technology. Our team has members with basic knowledge of C++, Python, DSA, HTML/CSS , Java and web development. We aim to work together and build an interactive and educational project for the NASA Space Apps Challenge.
summary: Lunar Outpost is a free browser game that trains kids aged 7 to 12 to run a Moon or Mars base. Players keep four meters alive (Life, Power, Shield, Food), walk inside a modular base, clean solar panels, fix life support, grow food, drive a rover and shelter from solar storms. It answers the challenge directly: every decision trades one real engineering need against another, so students feel why missions succeed or fail. The game uses real NASA data. Solar storm countdowns come from NASA DONKI coronal mass ejections, shown in a Sun Watch tool where each dot is a real CME. Sunrise, sunset, Mars season and Moon phase are computed for today's date, and live NASA images (Mars 2020, EPIC, SDO) appear with an honest Live or Archived label. Missions last 8, 14 or 24 sols, with upgrades, crew jobs, room-code multiplayer, a voice coach and full English and Hindi. It needs no install or account, so any classroom can use it.
details:
What it does: Lunar Outpost is a 3D browser game where a student commands a Moon or Mars outpost. You land (with a Martian-style parachute descent), walk into a long modular base, and keep Life, Power, Shield and Food above zero for 8, 14 or 24 sols. Tasks include cleaning solar panels, fixing life support, harvesting the greenhouse, driving the rover and beaming science to Earth. Solar storms arrive with a real countdown and the player must reach the storm shelter in time. On Mars, radio delay forces choices: decide now or wait for Mission Control. Solo players can assign jobs to crew or auto-assign. Friends can play together with a room code.

How it works and what we used: plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript with three.js (r128) for the 3D world, PeerJS for multiplayer, no backend. Real conditions come from our own code (js/space-env.js): Mars24 season and sun position, sunrise and sunset by latitude, Moon phase and Earth phase for today's date. js/nasa-live.js fetches live NASA images and js/donki.js fetches NASA DONKI space-weather data, each cached and labelled Live or Archived so nothing is faked. NASA 3D models (Viking lander, Lunar Module, rover, DSN dish) were compressed with gltf-transform and NASA logos were painted out of their textures.

Benefits and goal: kids learn that space missions are trade-offs between life support, power, radiation shielding and food, and why real solar storms matter. It is accessible (English and Hindi, voice coach, large text, free, no account). Creativity: a Martian-style landing, walk-in base interiors, real-sun day and night, and a Sun Watch tool that lets kids watch real CMEs travel toward the Moon and Mars. We hope teachers use it for a lesson on space weather and mission planning. Team Pheonix, Delhi, India.
